title: File Explorer .svg thumbnail preview plugin Memory Leak

fix_assessment.rationale: No current fix covers this single-file renderer hang. Issue #34491 addresses the general cost of creating a WebView2 instance for each SVG, while this report describes one supplied SVG exhausting memory; the current provider also waits without a render deadline. A bounded teardown is a plausible mitigation, but current-build reproduction must confirm its effectiveness.

proposed_fixes.title: Bound SVG thumbnail rendering and tear down hung WebView2 instances
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The reporter's SVG is reported to hang multiple browser engines, and the thumbnail provider signals completion only after navigation/capture or an initialization failure. Its wait loop has no deadline, so a renderer that never completes can keep the per-thumbnail host alive indefinitely and retain resources. Whether bounded teardown fully reclaims renderer memory remains to be verified.
plan: Add a finite deadline for WebView2 initialization and thumbnail rendering so a stalled navigation or capture returns no thumbnail instead of waiting indefinitely.
On timeout, safely dispose the WebView2 control and release its environment, and prevent any late asynchronous callback from using disposed state.
Add focused coverage for a render that never completes and verify the provider exits its wait and releases the renderer resources; retain the reporter's SVG as an isolated integration case.
verification: Run the focused SvgThumbnailProvider unit tests, including a controlled non-completing navigation case that verifies bounded return and cleanup.

In an isolated Windows test environment, reproduce with the reporter-provided SVG in Explorer using medium-or-larger icons; record provider/WebView2 memory and confirm the thumbnail request either completes or fails within the deadline without ongoing resource growth.
Compare the current supported build with the reported 0.88.0 behavior and distinguish a single-file render hang from the per-file startup cost tracked by issue #34491.

confidence.rationale: The issue supplies a specific SVG and reports unbounded WebView2 memory growth; a member also reports that the sample hangs other browsers. Current provider source has an unbounded completion wait, which supports a containment fix, but the issue has not been reproduced on a current supported build and timeout teardown has not been tested.

issue_context.summary: A specific SVG reportedly drives the Explorer thumbnail handler's WebView2 process memory upward until the machine runs out of RAM.
known_information: The report identifies PowerToys 0.88.0, Windows 11 24H2 build 26120.3281, and the File Explorer SVG thumbnail provider.
The reporter links a specific houndstooth SVG and says that placing it in an Explorer folder using medium-or-larger icons causes a WebView2 process to consume all available RAM.
A PowerToys maintainer reported that the same sample hangs Edge, Chrome, and Firefox and linked Chromium issue 398904328; the reporter supplied that Chromium issue URL.
Current `SvgThumbnailProvider.GetThumbnailImpl` waits in a loop until `thumbnailDone` is signaled and disposes the WebView2 control only after that wait; the loop has no timeout.
Issue #34491 concerns general SVG thumbnail throughput and the cost of a new WebView2 instance per file; its latest discussion does not establish a fix for this single-file memory-exhaustion report.
inferences: The sample's renderer workload may be the primary trigger because it reportedly stalls multiple browser engines, but this does not establish that PowerToys should accept indefinite resource use.
The provider's unbounded wait can keep a hung per-thumbnail host alive; a bounded teardown may contain the impact, but current-build behavior and cleanup effectiveness are unverified.
issue_context.analysis: Keep this report distinct from #34491: repeated WebView2 startup for many files is a throughput issue, while this report describes a single pathological SVG exhausting memory. Current source has no render deadline and blocks until a completion signal, supporting a narrow containment proposal rather than a replacement SVG renderer. Reproduce the supplied asset in an isolated current build and verify that a timed-out render releases its host and WebView2 resources before finalizing the design.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body and all five comments, including the reporter's request to reopen it separately from #34491, the maintainer's cross-browser reproduction observation, and the linked Chromium issue.

Inspected `src/modules/previewpane/SvgThumbnailProvider/SvgThumbnailProvider.cs`: WebView2 completion is signaled by navigation/capture or initialization failure, the wait loop at lines 211-214 has no deadline, and disposal follows the wait at lines 216-218.
Confirmed this provider file is unchanged between the current PR head and its upstream-main base; no fix for this issue is present in that source snapshot.
Compared #34491's latest discussion: it documents per-file WebView2 creation and general performance cost but does not establish coverage for this supplied-file memory exhaustion.
No current-build reproduction, memory capture, unit test, or verification of timeout cleanup has been performed.

information_gaps.information: Whether the supplied SVG still causes unbounded WebView2 memory growth on a current supported PowerToys build
information_gaps.why_needed: The report is from version 0.88.0, and a current reproduction is needed to confirm that the present handler still exhibits the behavior and that a render deadline would mitigate it.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: If available, test the same SVG on a current supported build and report the exact PowerToys and Windows versions plus whether WebView2 memory continues to grow; if it reproduces, add `/bugreport` immediately after Explorer stalls and before closing it.

judgment.rationale: The exact sample, reproduction path, cross-browser hang report, and current provider's unbounded wait support a concrete containment direction. A current-build reproduction and teardown test are still required, so the proposal remains yellow-confidence rather than a confirmed defect mechanism.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the supplied SVG in an isolated current build, then evaluate a bounded WebView2 render deadline and teardown; keep the issue separate from #34491's general per-file performance concern.
evidence: The issue reports that the linked SVG causes a WebView2 process to consume all available RAM when Explorer generates medium-or-larger thumbnails.
A maintainer reports that the sample hangs Edge, Chrome, and Firefox and points to Chromium issue 398904328, supporting a pathological renderer workload.
Current `GetThumbnailImpl` waits without a deadline for `thumbnailDone` and disposes the browser only after the wait completes.
Issue #34491's latest discussion is about the per-file WebView2 startup cost, not this reported single-file runaway-memory behavior.
The issue has not been reproduced on a current supported build, and no teardown test establishes that a timeout releases the renderer.

reproduce.title: Verify SVG thumbnail behavior with the reported houndstooth sample
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare the reported PowerToys 0.88.0 behavior with a current supported build.
prerequisites: Use an isolated Windows test environment because the report describes memory consumption up to all available RAM.
Enable the PowerToys SVG thumbnail handler and use the reporter-provided SVG linked in the issue.
setup: Place the reporter-provided SVG in a disposable test folder.
steps: Open the test folder in File Explorer and select medium-or-larger icons.
Record whether thumbnail generation completes and observe the PowerToys.SvgThumbnailProvider and msedgewebview2 process memory until it completes or stalls.
If safe, compare the same sample in the reported browser engines and record whether the renderer stalls there as described.
reproduce.expected_result: Determine whether the current thumbnail provider reproduces unbounded memory growth or an indefinitely incomplete request for this one file, separately from the per-file startup delay reported in issue #34491.
